blocks.prompt: 5 (i) If \(x\) is so small that its cube and higher power can be neglected, show that \(\sqrt{1 - x - 2x^{2}} \approx 1 - \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{9}{8}x^{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Cube and higher powers are neglected, so we keep terms up to \(x^{2}\).
The whole expression under the root, \(-x - 2x^{2}\), plays the role of \(y\) in \((1 + y)^{1/2}\).
Plan: expand to \(y^{2}\), substitute, keep powers up to \(x^{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(\sqrt{1 - x - 2x^{2}}\), \(x^{3}\) and higher powers negligible.
To show: \(\approx 1 - \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{9}{8}x^{2}\).
Method: Since \(x^{3}\) and higher powers are neglected, each series is kept up to its \(x^{2}\) term, and any product giving \(x^{3}\) or more is dropped.

Set up
\[\sqrt{1 - x - 2x^{2}} = (1 + y)^{1/2}\]
\[y = -x - 2x^{2}\]
Why: The bracket already starts with 1; everything after it is \(y\).

Expand up to \(y^{2}\)
\[(1 + y)^{1/2} \approx 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}y - \dfrac{1}{8}y^{2}\]
Why: \(y^{3}\) contains \(x^{3}\) and higher, so it is neglected.

Check
\[x = 0.1:\ \sqrt{0.88} = 0.938083\]
\[1 - 0.05 - 0.01125 = 0.93875\]
Why: The difference (about 0.0007) is of the size of the neglected \(x^{3}\) terms.

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) If \(x\) is so small that its cube and higher power can be neglected, show that \(\sqrt{\frac{1 + x}{1 - x}} \approx 1 + x + \frac{1}{2}x^{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Keep terms up to \(x^{2}\).
Write the left side as \((1 + x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-1/2}\), expand each to \(x^{2}\), multiply.
Plan: two series of three terms, multiply, keep powers up to \(x^{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(\sqrt{\frac{1 + x}{1 - x}}\), \(x^{3}\) and higher powers negligible.
To show: \(\approx 1 + x + \frac{1}{2}x^{2}\).
Method: Since \(x^{3}\) and higher powers are neglected, each series is kept up to its \(x^{2}\) term, and any product giving \(x^{3}\) or more is dropped.

Write as a product
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}} = (1 + x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-1/2}\]
Why: \(\sqrt{\tfrac{a}{b}} = a^{1/2}b^{-1/2}\).

Multiply, keeping up to \(x^{2}\)
\[x: \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1\]
\[x^{2}: \dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow 1 + x + \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\]
Why: \(x^{2}\) comes from \(1 \cdot \tfrac{3}{8}x^{2}\), \(\tfrac{1}{2}x \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}x\) and \(-\tfrac{1}{8}x^{2} \cdot 1\).

Check
\[x = 0.1:\ \sqrt{\dfrac{1.1}{0.9}} = 1.105542\]
\[1 + 0.1 + 0.005 = 1.105\]
Why: The difference (about 0.0005) is of the size of the neglected \(x^{3}\) term.
